HotHands Hand Warmers - Long Lasting Safe Natural Odorless Air Activated Warmers - Up to 10 Hours of Heat - 40 Pair I was at work one day. I work retail and our store is always FREEZING due to them not wanting to turn the heat on in order to save themselves money. I went into work one morning while it was -7 degrees outside. My store was obviously not as cold as outside, but like I said they refuse to turn on the heat so it's pretty cold in the store as well.

Anyway, I was standing at my register waiting for customers to come by. While waiting another employee asked "Are you cold?" and I replied that I was and that my hands were the most cold, so she handed me hot hands, which immediately wowed me! It was so warm the second I put my hands on it and it really helped me out between customers for quite a number of hours. She allowed me to keep it, thankfully, so I was able to see how long it would last. It lasted throughout my entire shift and basically the rest of the day.

I plan to buy more of these because normally my hands get dry and start to bleed when they are exposed to cold air for too long at my job (yes, I know it sounds crazy that my store is this cold. Trust me, I believe it is crazy as well to force employees and customers to stand it ... I get customers complaining to me every day that it is too cold in the store). But anyway, I just have to tolerate the super cold air in my store. If I purchase these and use them each time it'll help me out quite a bit. I highly recommend these to anyone who has to put up with exposing their hands to cold air for long periods of time.

text_fidelity_a:
MOON LENCE 2 PCS Body Boards for Beach Lightweight with EPS Core & Wrist Leash 33/37/41" Body Board with Slick Bottom Surfing for Kids Teens and Adults My wife and I love going to the beach and had been wanting body boards for a long time. So when I had the chance, I grabbed these MOON LENCE Body Board - we are thrilled with them! Ok, maybe we’re just big kids at heart, but that’s the way life should be, so riding the waves is a lot of fun and today we spent a couple hours on these boards. From start to finish it was a great time and we can’t wait to go back... except, we are pretty sure this was the last weekend it’ll be warm enough even in our hot weather state, so yea, we wish we’d gotten them earlier, but no worry, we’ll have them for next year (or next weekend with any luck).

They are a great set - two is always better than one when you’ve got two people as you don’t have to share. We went with the yellow because let’s face it, they’re easy to see - they really are! The materials are excellent. The front has a slight texture that feels good - meaning you’re not scratched or feel rough when laying on it - and it lets you have a better grip. We had decent waves today and never once felt like we didn’t not have control. The back is smooth and rides the wave well. It is so well designed and done - compared to others we have looked at and not bought - that we would most certainly look at more in the future from the same line. I”m a bit heavier at present and I was still able to get the waves - though we could not get out as far and I was dropping deeper than my wife so had to watch in the shallower waters. The strap for your wrist was great. My wife put them on - they come unattached - and did mention it’s threading the needle - needs a soft touch, yet easy to do. Once on they STAYED ON! I mean you’d have thought these were pro boards or something they felt, looked, and rode so well. It was a bit of an effort getting the velcro undone the first time - we both ended up pulling from the inside to get it open - but in the end, they stayed secured to us as the waves let us have it. We had a great time today - and as mentioned above, hope we get maybe another weekend out there. Thrilled to have these MOON LENCE Body Boards!
text_fidelity_b: MOON LENCE 2 PCS Body Boards for Beach Lightweight with EPS Core & Wrist Leash 33/37/41" Body Board with Slick Bottom Surfing for Kids Teens and Adults

text_fidelity_a:
Merrithew at Home SPX Reformer Bundle There are several issues here to consider prior to purchasing.

1. Will the carriage roll smoothly? Even after cleaning the rails, my stott SPX failed to roll smoothly. This is a really important point.

2. Are the hand/foot loops large enough to accommodate normal sized, adult hands and feet? My stott SPX came with super tiny hand/feet loops that wouldn't work for a six year old, let alone an adult. And I have very small, adult hands.

3. Is the carriage padding sufficient? My stott SPX arrived with very thin padding and it hurt the back during movements.

4. Is this the best price on the market? Absolutely not. This package sells elsewhere on the internet for up to $500 less with additional dvd's included.

5. Will stott respond to inquiries? My phone calls and emails were ignored. It's as if this company only responds to large commercial accounts. You're completely on your own and out of luck if there is a problem or if you have a question.

6. Is the delivery box manageable? My stott SPX came in one box, approximately 14 feet long. Inside this massive box there were a couple smaller boxes. But you're talking something akin to tremendous problems getting it from curbside into the house, and if like me, you return it for being an incredible waste of money and a huge disappointment, it is painful to deal with a 14 foot box that won't fit into any normal car or suv. Hope you have a truck handy.

7. Check out other reformer brands. For a little more money the quality soars. You might think cheap is ok now, but you won't use a poor quality reformer in the long run.
text_fidelity_b: Merrithew at Home SPX Reformer Bundle

text_fidelity_a:
Bushnell 14MP Trophy Cam HD Aggressor Low Glow Trail Camera, Brown I was looking forward to having found a good camera here, but disappointed. Similar to a sister company's Primos 02 camera that I tried, I found that the field of the motion sensor was misaligned with the field of the picture. I determined this by walking past the camera to observe the results. Consequently, animals to the right of the picture field of view would set it off and you might not get them in a picture at all. And animals walking from left to right would not trigger it until well past center of the picture. The Primos 02 misalignment was worse but the Bushnell wasn't good.

On the positive, the pictures and videos from this camera were very good; superior to the Primos 02 and another camera I tried. The wide screen picture was perfect for my use. The settings allow for both shutter speed and LED intensity which certainly should be useful to adjust for how far away your primary target area is. It is because of the picture quality that I thought I had found the right camera for me. The Hybrid feature to take both pictures followed by videos is great. Unlike the Primos 02, I didn't have excessive false positive pictures.

But then, I changed the shutter speed and LED settings to take pictures on a closer target area which resulted in the camera taking pictures and videos constantly, nearly 1000 in a 24 hour period. If the "Field Scan" were set to ON, that might have been the result but I had it set to OFF. Of course, two days of this drained the batteries.

Another difficulty is that when set to take three burst pictures, the delay was too quick. Per the time stamp, all three would snap within a single second and you cannot adjust this. So your animal hardly had any time to move further through the field of view.

The camera came with current firmware, so an older version firmware was not to blame for these issues. Possibly the product was defective but I returned it for refund rather than exchange, largely because with my Primos 02 experience an exchange of cameras did not fix the misalignment.
text_fidelity_b: Bushnell 14MP Trophy Cam HD Aggressor Low Glow Trail Camera, Brown

MASXODRK Universal Scooter Bag,Waterproof and Stable Handlebar Bag for Scooter/EBike/Motorcycle/Bicycle,Large Capacity&Portable EVA Scooter Accessories Storage Bag for Charger,Repair Tools&Phone I fully admit, we got this MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag for our two unknown/lesser known brand eScooters not knowing if we had a chance for it to fit. It is not one of the ones listed on the product page, so... in the end, it has worked out great on both our eScooters, so we are happy to have it.

This MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag has two straps at the top to go on the handlebars, two on the back to wrap and hold it to the upright stick of the eScooter. But would there be enough room between/around/next too the break and accelerator? For both of ours, yes. They fit slightly differently, but yes, we got them on there, no problem. The straps on the back - one over the other - holds the bag to the stick perfectly. The top ones come with such a long piece of material, you have various options on length down the front stick - we can actually do it at varying heights and simply wrap the remaining material. The ones on the back are a little more limited, but not so much that we could not also adjust - here it was how tight to make it against the stick, and this varied by how high or low we did the top one. In other words, there is enough material on the top two straps that it allowed us to adjust the placement of the bag on the two different eScooters, and on each eScooter itself, for more overall options.

The bag is a good size. We can get both wallets, a phone or two, keys, all in there. The velcro holds it strong enough. And we are good to go. We do NOT ride in any weather, so no idea how it would handle rain - but we never want to find out. We THINK it would be okay and keep stuff good. There is a solid, type material for the shell, cloth for the edges, all SHOULD hold back the rain - but that cloth COULD potentially get soaked and leaked. But our understanding of eScooters - you'd have a bigger problem with the scooter getting wet first.

In the end we are thrilled with this MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag and while we are using it on our eScooters, we feel it would go on a bike or other item as well, depending on the design of course, but opens more options for using it. We're thrilled.
text_fidelity_b: MASXODRK Universal Scooter Bag,Waterproof and Stable Handlebar Bag for Scooter/EBike/Motorcycle/Bicycle,Large Capacity&Portable EVA Scooter Accessories Storage Bag for Charger,Repair Tools&Phone

STAR BRITE Ultimate Citrus Cleaner & Degreaser - 32 OZ (096432) I went outside this morning to find that a vulture had strafed our new Honda CRV. One of the many hazards in Southwest Florida is the abundance of bird droppings from several relatively large species, with the vultures and pelicans giving the most bang for the buck. Sometimes I swear that these birds know when you have a new car in the driveway.

I always spray the offended area with a mist from our hose and let it sit for about a minute to help break up the chalky residue from bird poop. Afterwards you can apply a quick shot of any good quality cleaner and degreaser, let it soak in for another minute, and then wipe away gently with a clean cloth.

This Star Brite works well on this particular problem but I wouldn't categorize the product as being "ultimate". However I was pleasantly surprised when I used it to clean the burned on grease on our countertop burners. It was just a simple matter of spraying a bit on, letting it sit for a bit, and then scraping the residue off with a razorblade.

The only thing that I have found that works better cleaning cooktops is the Cerama Bryte Complete Cooktop Cleaning Kit which sells for about $2.00 more for the kit. However the Cerama Bryte cleaner is less useful on other projects around the house. The Star Brite smells better and gives you 32 oz. of a more 'all purpose' formula to use.
text_fidelity_b: STAR BRITE Ultimate Citrus Cleaner & Degreaser - 32 OZ (096432)

text_fidelity_a: MICLON Cybertrack 100 Electric Bike for Adults, 2X Faster Charge, 350W BAFANG Motor, 36V 10.4AH Removable Battery, 20MPH 26'' Mountain Ebike, Shimano 21 Speed, Suspension Fork, LED Display I'm a 75 year old man who has been riding a regular bike for years and years but my knees were telling me that hills were no longer their friend. I moved from a place with NO hills to a place where hills are everywhere so I decided to look in to an ebike that was within my budget. This bike seemed to be just what I needed so I decided to give it a shot...First thing was it was very easy to assemble (Youtube helped)..then I decided to take it for a spin. This bike is a completely different experience so my advise would be to practice in a place that's deserted...so here's the low down on my first week of riding on a regular basis....first, this bike will get up and go and reach 20 mph very fast, and for me that was my first surprise, then getting a feel for the 5 levels of resistance 1 being the most and 5 is where you hardly pedal at all, but here's where you need to pay attention....the throttle takes up about half the right handle bar so it's very easy to accelerate when you don't want to so pay attention...then there the issue with the kick stand which seems be very wobblily and a little unstable....having said that, I really like this bike, it's very easy and fun when you get used to it...quick note, I would not leave my house with charger plugged it just to be safe...So now on July 13th or having the bike for over a month the only thing that is driving me nuts is the kick stand...it flops down over and over again even after tightening the so called locking mechanism..it is aggravating and turns my bike ride into a hassle.....it's a terrible TERRIBLE design....................*******.........So I've  owned the bike almost 4 months and I continue to love this bike, I replaced the kick stand and replaced the seat with one a lot more comfortable, The one thing that, for me, makes the ride safer and more predictable is....if I'm riding near people or on roads with intersections I keep the resistance on 1 or 0 and use the hand throttle to provide power to the bike. I used to keep it on 2-4 but found that when I wanted to stop if any pressure was put on the pedals when trying to stop immediately throws the bike forward when you're not expecting it..I learned the hard way and it wasn't pretty..In my opinion controlling the bike with the hand throttle is the safest except if your riding on a trail or on a road with no stop and go...This in my opinion is the best and safest way to operate the bike with the electric assist....aside from that this is a great entry level bike at a very good price.  I look forward to many more miles of fun...
text_fidelity_b: MICLON Cybertrack 100 Electric Bike for Adults, 2X Faster Charge, 350W BAFANG Motor, 36V 10.4AH Removable Battery, 20MPH 26'' Mountain Ebike, Shimano 21 Speed, Suspension Fork, LED Display

text_fidelity_a: Edge 61135-7 H20 Quiver Magnet These little decoy aids are great, but you have to do a couple of things before you use them, or you will experience the problems others noted. 1. spray the switch, motor and battery contacts with a good Teflon oil. 2. get a package of Remington Camo wrap and cut to fit the top of the cover 3. be sure to tighten the lid securely.  I hunt a very natural blind with about 2 dozen decoys positioned in sets of six and I add three of these aids to each set. For storage and ease of setup, I keep them on slip rigs in sets of three separated with a D ring for each three.  As another hunter noted, they are not intended to move your decoys, but to add some motion to the water within your decoy set.  I can tell you they do make a big difference in bringing in the ducks, especially on still days.  When needed, take the time to replace the batteries at the end of the days hunt and you'll be ready for the next hunt.  One final tip, don't forget that mallards and other puddle ducks only feed in water 12" to 15" deep or less, and these aids mimic a feeding duck.
text_fidelity_b: Edge 61135-7 H20 Quiver Magnet

text_fidelity_a:
SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black There is a major difference between this tube and its non thorn-resistant counterparts. The difference translates to a 3x larger package and a 3x stiffer inner tube. Whether this means that it will intercede on your behalf when penetrating objects attempt to derail your day, time will tell. But I can tell you that:

1) It takes some effort to stuff this piece of salami into your tire. It doesn't bend willingly.
2) It takes some getting used to on the road. Your tire will absorb less shock from road imperfections, resulting in a harsh ride. It's not like riding on solid rubber, but it's not as soft as a regular inner tube.

In my opinion, the harsh ride is worth it on a daily commuter, where reliability is paramount. I'm not sure if I'd use this on a recreational bike. A suspension bike may be fine.

Update: after a week or two, I stopped noticing the stiffer ride quality. Also, I have about 50lbs extra on that rear wheel, so my experience may not be typical (it's an e-bike).
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black

I bought a pair and like most, did not test them on ice. I mean, unless you live in Canada/Alaska you usually have them for months before you get to wear them out in inclement conditions (purchase Winter boots in the Summer for the best prices!)

Well, everything was fine - boots were great - until I hit my first patch of ice. Something about the sole material caused me to slip and slide like a drunkard... I was about to relegate the boots to the closet when I saw these crampons were available. Amazing!

The crampons I know about are from nature shows I've seen on TV. Huge spikes. Only put on when you reach the icy end of the Earth... Whereas these crampons are GREAT for walking around the city in snowy weather. Or the day after a snow when daylight heating and nighttime freezing have created a tremendous number of icy patches.

They have given my step confidence. Literally.

Recommended!
text_fidelity_b: Doormoon Crampons, Walk Cleats Traction Ice Grips for Boots Shoes Anti Slip with 10 Spikes for Snowing Hiking Ice Fishing Mountaineering

text_fidelity_a:
Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black Just installed the Mirrycle bicycle mirror today and took it for a test run.

A few observations and comments.

Agreed, assembly is not entirely easy. As mentioned by numerous reviews, the screws drive hard to the point that you think you’re actually cracking the plastic plus the included Allen wrench requires some strength to turn. But not to worry. Read the instructions and they’ll confirm the hard drive and that you will not crack the plastic. I didn’t try WD40 or any other lubricant so cannot say if that would ease the assembly.

I installed the Mirrycle onto a GT hybrid bicycle and after using a Dremel tool to create an opening in the end of my handle grip I found the handlebar opening accepted the smaller of the two wedges for mounting. I chose to follow the alternative down and under installation mentioned on Amazon reviews which is quite clever and works very well however I believe you may get a better site picture using the “normal” above and to the side installation which would facilitate not having to move your eyes so far from your frontal path to do so. The primary disadvantage to the “normal” up-and-out installation is that the mirror really sticks out there very exposed and if/when you dump your bike or ride close to any shrubs, etc., your mirror will be the early casualty, plus the storage shed where we keep our bikes is small which would necessitate tucking the mirror in upon each return. Do whichever works best for you.

From the lower mounting position I could see both myself and directly behind me but I don’t believe that provides the maximum field of view. On my initial trip I stopped a couple times to adjust the mirror in a similar manner to what you would do with a car, i.e., if you can see part of yourself/your bike in the mirror, tilt it out just a little further until you can’t and that should be about right. Once adjusted properly you only need to tilt your head a tad one way to see either part of yourself directly behind the mirror or a tad the other way to see much more of the road to your direct left.

I was amazed at how solid this mirror rode exhibiting absolutely no jitter or vibration. The large convex shape offered a wide, clear field of view which allowed me not only to see what was coming from behind me but also what was to the near left rear of me as well.

This was only my first day with this product but I’m impressed with the quality and the flexible mounting options it offers.
text_fidelity_b: Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black

The paintwork is cheap, the head is a generic design that shows up in other mfrs' clubs (albeit at a higher price) and its overall feel doesn't lend one to believe it'll hold up more than a couple seasons.  Most crucially, though, I've taken mine out a fair amount in the last six weeks and it already shows clear signs of stress fracturing and surface cracking on the face, right around the sweet spot.  I hit a consistent 270-280 yard drive with the club - for now.  But I don't hold much hope it's a club that'll live long if used often.
text_fidelity_b: King Par TEC Plus 460 cc Ti Matrix Driver Men's

text_fidelity_a:
SANLIKE Fishing Reel Baitcasting Reel for Saltwater Freshwater, Magnet Dual Braking Force Bait Casting Reel, Ultra Smooth 17.6 Lb Carbon Fiber Drag - 6.3:1 Gear Ratio - Right Hand I know the SAN Like Baitcasting Fishing Reel is advertised for salt water foremost...but I can't see it. To my way of thinking it's more of a lightweight bass reel. And it is light and small of frame. Two hours after I got mine I was on a local public lake trying it out. Been looking forward to it.

Size-wise it would be at home on a lighter rod if that's your notion. I mated mine to an old comfy Speed Stick. First thing I noticed was the spool isn't solid. It has holes in it. I'm sure there is a more scientific way to say it but I don't know what it is. A small matter, but it makes tying the line onto it much easier, as you can pass it through the holes. Next up, something I haven't seen before...the drag 'clicks' as you adjust it. An improvement, I think, as it gives more finesse to the operation. Otherwise the reel behaves much as any other.

I have a ton of reels. Some mine, some hand-me-downs. Some are top o' the line too. But one thing I have noticed...high dollar or low dollar they ALL wear out just the same. Point being that since this is the case for the money, you can't do better with high dollar than you can with the SAN Like Baitcasting Fishing Reel. If you're just starting out you can purchase 3 or 4 for less than you'll spend on one of the big names. Functionally there isn't much difference and like I said, they all have a lifespan. Heck, rod and reel makers could give away their products to sell their branded lures. That's where all your money is going anyway.

One tip. The brake knob. On power casts with mine time and again at the apex I'd get that professional overlap thing. My reel, at any rate, is pretty finicky about having enough resistance. Typically you set that knob so your bait drops slowly and that's it. But this reel needs a bit more braking... then it works like a charm. So if you get a tangle, just run that knob up a bit more. You'll still be able to get that bait way out there without the birds nest effect.

Only time and use will tell how my new reel holds up, but for my money, I'm tickled with it. It's as much as I hoped for and nary a complaint. I'd love to see some validation with good reviews.
text_fidelity_b: SANLIKE Fishing Reel Baitcasting Reel for Saltwater Freshwater, Magnet Dual Braking Force Bait Casting Reel, Ultra Smooth 17.6 Lb Carbon Fiber Drag - 6.3:1 Gear Ratio - Right Hand

text_fidelity_a: Power Pro Spectra Fiber Braided Fishing Line I LOVE this fishing line. not only is it a good color that blends in well with most fishing environments, but it's crazy strong! I have hauled in some heavy game fish and even an actual SEAL when fishing from the ocean once. lol (which was obviously released soon after landing it) but this line can handle just about anything you can throw at it. I can't always say the same for the rods or reels, but the line rarely ever snaps. I love that it is such a low profile line too. Like the diameter of the line is far thinner than the comparable monofilament version, and MUCH easier to tie than the thick plastic stuff. I find the plastic monofilament stuff is harder to get the knot to hold than the braided lines. Yes it is certainly far more expensive than the monofilament ones, but in my personal opinion, it is worth every penny to pay that little extra and rarely ever have to worry about losing that lunker because your line snapped. I have seen the hooks BEND before this line snaps, which to me is pretty darned impressive.

Tuff Products QuickStrips Reloading Strips for Revolvers Size 6357 Orange This is a great way to carry extra ammo for your concealed carry weapon. They are easy to load, lie flat in your pocket, and easy to take out when reloading. It sure beats using a bulky speed loader. Yes, the speed loader is quicker, but your chances of needing more than eight shots to defend yourself is minimal.

Eight shots you ask? I bit the bullet (so to speak) and purchased a Smith and Wesson .357 Magnum Model 327 Performance Center, an eight shot revolver. It is a scandium snub nose that holds .38 specials, 38 + P, and .357 magnums. Light but bulky, it fits my large hands well and the recoil (even under full magnum loads) is manageable. Expensive but unique, it is a gun that will become a collector item in the future. Not many revolvers can hold eight large bullets.

And yes, it is a wheel gun for personal protection. My first gun purchase 41 years ago was a Ruger Blackhawk in .44 magnum, carried while salmon fishing in Alaska. I also own a Smith and Wesson .44 magnum Alaskan, another snub nose revolver. So recoil isn't an issue for me. Why a revolver instead of one of the excellent semi autos out there? If I ever need to use it to protect myself or my family, I need to know that it will go BANG when I pull the trigger. I also need to know that my spouse can use it without fumbling around.. Just aim it and pull the trigger. And then again, and again. The simplicity and "bullet proof" action inspires confidence -- especially when you find yourself in a very stressful situation.

My backup piece is also a revolver that will handle the same three calibers. Just in case. Kinda like wearing a belt and suspenders. Redundancy is not a bad thing in personal protection.
text_fidelity_b: Tuff Products QuickStrips Reloading Strips for Revolvers Size 6357 Orange

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) My first one wouldn't hold a charge for longer than a day and a half, but I was able to rather easily get a refund for that one, and purchase a brand new one.

I use the iPhone app almost exclusively, since the Windows program is inexcusably bad. Theoretically any device with Bluetooth 4.0 should be able to talk to the Charge, but my Android tablet was unable to, so until I got my iPhone I was forced to use the Windows program along with a small USB FitBit dongle.

The Windows program has absolutely no other function then to sync with the Charge, Which in theory you can do anytime that the charge is within range. But my installation of Windows 7 ultimate was unable to perform this task without me specifically launching the program and telling it to sync.

With the exception of doing a little of the initial setup, other than that single function of retrieving information from the Charge, passing it on to the FitBit website and vice-versa, the Windows desktop program does nothing. Literally nothing.

The fact that the desktop app does nothing, forces you forces the users without a FitBit compatible phone or tablet to perform everything that ought to be able to be doable locally on the webpage.

Things like, choosing a watch face, or determining the order in which things are displayed, or determining what, if anything, a double tap on the watch face does.

Some other useful changes I would like to see are:

+ Personally, since the FitBit communicates via Bluetooth, I see no reason why the FitBit Bluetooth dongle that comes with the device can't be used by the computer that you plug it into as a Bluetooth dongle. They just need to write drivers specific to their dongle, which they already have, that have a way of seizing control of the dongle when it needs to transmit, and then return control of the dongle to the regular Bluetooth system when it's done. We've already paid for the Bluetooth dongle, we might as well be able to use it, even if we only ever use the app.

+ Most usefully, change the clock faces to show:
1) Remaining battery charge! (Could just be asterisks, periods, or even the pipe symbol | .)
2) The Day of the Week!
3) The Date! (MM/DD)
4) Option to display AM/PM with 12 hour watch faces.

+ Add the "Connected GPS" that the new Blaze boast's!

+ Of course, change the desktop program so that you can do all the things that you can do on both the website and the apps, on your computer.

+ Changing how the app displays your sleep data so that it includes the amount of time that you slept deeply, or were in interrupted sleep.

+ Making the website more intuitive.
+ Have the website display your sleep data in a useful manner.

+ A larger range of watch faces to choose from, not just the current four.
+ The option of an analog watch face.
+ Add a screen to the charge that displays at least some of your sleep data.
+ Allow the Charge to be accessed via Bluetooth, so that even phones unable to install the fit bit app can still send text and caller and information to it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a:
Eafengrow EF953 Pocket Folding Knife G10 Handle D2 Blade,EDC Tool Knife for Outdoor Camping Hiking (Black) NGL, it's a slick looking knife, but it isn't well constructed.

The blade looks good and the scales feel good in the hand. The blade definitely is sharp. The issue is the pivot point of the knife and the scales around the pivot point.

You'll notice that there is a nice index finger groove up near the pivot point. This is a nice ergo component, however when gripping the knife here the scales flex and cause a severe amount of blade play at the pivot point. Inversely, grabbing the blade towards the base and wigging it will cause the scales at that finger well to flex.

As much as I would like to write this off as a 1-off construction issue, I had an unrelated individual talk about the very same issue they had with this knife. They had sourced the knife from their local B&M and had mentioned the issue. I told them I had one in the mail and would check it when the knife showed up. Sure enough 2 instances of this knife with the same issue.

So buyer beware. I have heard good things about this knife maker and this knife so I decided to test the waters with this blade. I will be sending this knife back and I doubt I will be buying another Eafengrow even if it's another G-10 D2 for sub $20.
text_fidelity_b: Eafengrow EF953 Pocket Folding Knife G10 Handle D2 Blade,EDC Tool Knife for Outdoor Camping Hiking (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Fishing On The Fly | Fly Fishing Reel | High-Grade Aluminum Alloy | 3/4, 5/6, 7/8 Weights | Black I ordered this Fishing on the Fly reel for a couple of reasons. The reel I keep my sinking line on took a dump last time I was on the water, and I needed something to replace it. I went with this because of its clicking on retrieve (my preference), it's design, and of course, its price.
It reviewed well, and I figured that even if half of what people said were true, it would be a decent reel for the "price" as people always say.
This isn't just a decent reel "at the price"; it's a nice reel. It would be a nice reel at twice the price, and perhaps even at 2.5x the price. I used to work at a big box Outfitter outlet with a tin green roof, and this EXACT reel, with a better known branding and packaging, sold for more than twice the price. And I sold a lot of them.

The reel is tight, tolerances are close, setting the drag is positive and tactile, and it's light yet sturdy feeling. It handles fish very well, and stripping line out feels good.

I like the packaging, I love the little felt reel bag, and there's a form letter from the company owner that makes it sound like he is rely interested in the customer being happy with the product. And even though the reel is made in China, the literature included is in English. Proper English that wasn't just run through Google Translate. If I were to have an issue with this reel (which I don't foresee), I get the impression he would want to make it right.

My wife bought this reel for me, so even though this isn't a "confirmed purchase" out whatever it's called, we did pay for this, and I'm glad we did!

Basically stated, I like this reel a lot. I'll buy another one. The only thing I'd like to see is other color options. That's really the only complaint I'd want to see addressed in a reel of this build quality at anywhere below $90. You can't go wrong picking one of these up!
text_fidelity_b: Fishing On The Fly | Fly Fishing Reel | High-Grade Aluminum Alloy | 3/4, 5/6, 7/8 Weights | Black

DeskCycle Under Desk Bike Pedal Exerciser - Mini Exercise Bike Desk Cycle, Leg Exerciser for Physical Therapy & Desk Exercise - Adjustable Leg and Standard Versions I am a software engineer that sits at a desk for at least 8 hours a day. I wanted to way to keep my body from being idle for so many hours and also was looking for a way to help with my weight loss goals. The Deskcycle has been a fantastic solution. I pedal off and on throughout the day at a low setting (resistance of 3 right now) and try to aim for 50 miles at the end of the day (disclaimer: actual mileage seems a bit high to me but I don’t really care if it is accurate). Some days I up the resistance to push my legs a bit more and shoot for a lower distance. I am a 54 year old woman trying to lose 50+ pounds. In the past, even with healthy eating and routine workouts, my weight has been slow to come off (maybe a few pounds a month). Since I purchased the Deskcycle, I have lost 10 pounds in a month. I don’t know that I can credit the Deskcycle for this substantial increase, but it does feel like it is helping. I love it so much I am thinking of purchasing a second one to use for the days I work at home. I find myself feeling lazy if I haven’t pedaled throughout the day.

Pros:
Very easy setup
Easy to see and use electronic monitor with variety of settings to watch
Very low height requirements compared to other under desk bikes
10 resistance settings – can set to 3 or 4 and pedal good part of day or set higher for smaller bursts of pedaling
Can pedal forward or backward to hit different leg muscles
Very quiet (Coworker in next cubicle cannot hear it.)
Smooth motion, no clunkiness

Cons
Pricey compared to other under desk bikes
Takes a bit to get distance from chair adjusted

*The cons to me a well worth the benefits! The price is higher because it is much higher quality exerciser and will likely last longer as a result. The adjustment issue is one you would have on any desk bike.
text_fidelity_b: DeskCycle Under Desk Bike Pedal Exerciser - Mini Exercise Bike Desk Cycle, Leg Exerciser for Physical Therapy & Desk Exercise - Adjustable Leg and Standard Versions

I have never ridden a brooks saddle or leather saddle before but I would not rate this as comfortable. The cutout and overall size of the seat felt right, I just couldn't get past the very firm feel of the material.  Immediately after sitting on it I could feel my sit bones making direct contact with the material and the material not offering any sense of relief.  I did give this saddle about 40 miles before deciding it was not for me. I will admit the seat seemed to maintain the same level of comfort for the entire trip which is an improvement over other saddles I've owned, which become unbearable after 20 miles.  This saddle never felt unbearable no matter the time spent on it.  I am a large guy, weighing in at 220 lbs, which is what I am attributing to my issue. I did replace it with a gel saddle and it initially feels much better.  I have a feeling if you carry less weight, the lack of padding might work for you.

text_fidelity_a: PONOSOON Polarized Sports Sunglasses for Men Women for Cycling Running Fishing Golf TR90 Frame 007 (Black Frame Red Tips&Red Lens) I've been wearing these glasses now for a couple of weeks.  I don't use them for cycling or sports but rather more general day to day use like driving.  I really like the fit of these glasses.  They sit level on my face and are comfortable around my ear (meaning they don't squeeze too hard.  The tint is on the darker side - which I prefer because my eyes are very sensitive to light.  Quality is about what I'd expect in a $20 pair of sunglasses... maybe a little better.  Definitely not $5 cheap.  Looking through the lens, again is about what you expect for a $20 pair of polarized sunglasses.  I have other $20 glasses that have a crisper look but these are by no means bad.  When it is bright and sunny I can see clearer with them.  When it is more cloudy or overcast some of that crispness is lost.  If you keep in mind that these cost $20 bucks, the fit is good and comfortable, don't feel cheap and the lens make objects a little crisper then you will like these.  If you are looking for am $80 pair of glasses at a quarter of the price, these are not for you.  Its all relative.
text_fidelity_b: PONOSOON Polarized Sports Sunglasses for Men Women for Cycling Running Fishing Golf TR90 Frame 007 (Black Frame Red Tips&Red Lens)

For the difference in price we thought we'd give the Rubbermaid a try to see how it would perform.

The lower spigot on the Rubbermaid is solid. No leaks and easy to use. The upper vent spigot is a little bit of a weak point. It works absolutely fine, just remember to always close it so it doesn't get broken or let hot air cycle into the cold interior of the jug.

Although not an "extreme" cooler jug, once filled with ice and water we had cold water well into the second day in the desert. The cooler was kept in the shade the entire time.

If you need a rough and tumble water jug, look elsewhere. If you need something that will sit on a picnic table for a day or two, this will work fine.
